newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices end up on rebound.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices end up on rebound.

text.p: China's A and B share indices ended up on Monday on a rebound extending from Friday following recent falls brought about by Beijing's tough crackdown on excessive speculation, brokers said.

The Shanghai B index rose 1.288 points or 1.53 percent to 85.219 points on volume of 12.933 million shares worth $8.648 million and the Shenzhen B share index gained 2.96 points or 2.02 percent to 149.12 on turnover of HK$65 million.
Institutions were seen supporting shares with a heavy index weighting including Pudong real estate shares in the Shanghai market, brokers said.
But trading volume was thin with most investors sidelined waiting for the listing of Jinan Qingqi Motorcycle Co's 230 million B shares on Tuesday, they said.
"The rebound of domestic A share market sparked a little speculative buying, which pushed the B index up, but trading remained dull with most investors cautious to follow," said one broker.

The Shanghai A index rose 18.210 points or 1.40 percent to 1,317.132 on volume of 457.9 million shares worth 6.2 billion yuan. The SSE30 blue chip index went up 54.396 points or 1.42 percent to 3,879.783 points.
"Most investors are waiting for the listing of Jinan Qingqi and its performance will have great impact on the short-term market direction with its huge capitalisation," another broker said.
The series of crackdown measures had been discounted by the markets, which appear to have bottomed out temporarily according to the technical charts, brokers said.

The clampdown measures included barring state enterprises from involvement in speculative trading, imposing tough penalities on banks and replace Zhou Daojiong, the chief of its top stock market watchdog China Securities Regulatory Commission.

"Investors think the worst of the negative news has emerged and they started buying in anticipation of no further bad news at least over the short term," an analyst with Jardine Fleming Securities Ltd in Shenzhen said.

"More investors now seem to be interpreting Beijing's recent clampdown as being aimed at fostering the long-term healthy development of the market rather than just bad news for equity investors," a broker at China Guotai Securities said.
Construction machinery maker Shanghai Jintai was the star on the Shanghai B share market on the basis of one speculative buy, soaring $0.012 or 9.23 percent to $0.142 on thin volume of 1,000 shares.
Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Development was the most actively traded on institutional support, gaining $0.002 or 0.23 percent to $0.860 on volume of 1.7 million shares.
In Shenzhen, toll road operator Guangdong Provincial Expressway was the best B share performer, surging HK$0.70 to its ten percent limit up level at HK$7.68.
The Shenzhen A share index jumped 12.03 points or 2.79 percent to end at 443.12 on turnover of 8.1 billion yuan against 7.0 billion yuan last Friday.
